title: Tallypad — quick experiment digest
content:
Purpose: tiny running log of quick A/B runs I do on my dev node. Keep numbers + config + first impressions. Not polished — notes to self.

Quick summary (so I don't re-run same set):
- Goal: find cheap config that keeps p95 < 300ms for common 256-token prompts.
- Context: 1xA10G dev box, local build of runtime v0.23, KV caching toggled in middle runs.
- Best inexpensive config so far: t1 (int8 q4) + batch 4 + prefix cache = decent tradeoff.

Experiment table (columns: date | model | quant | batch | seq | prefix_cache | tokens/s | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | $/1k tokens est | notes)

2025-02-11 | redwood-owl-7b | q8_ggml | 1 | 256 | off | 8.9 | 120 | 420 | 0.008 | baseline, no cache, low throughput, p95 spikes on long context
2025-02-12 | redwood-owl-7b | q4_int8 | 4 | 256 | off | 28.4 | 95 | 310 | 0.003 | batch helps a lot, p95 still a bit high occasionally
2025-02-14 | redwood-owl-7b | q4_int8 | 4 | 256 | on | 40.1 | 78 | 190 | 0.0022 | prefix cache reduced p95 by ~40%, cost down
2025-02-18 | redwood-raven-13b | q4_int8 | 2 | 256 | on | 18.6 | 140 | 360 | 0.006 | higher quality but cost/latency jump; try smaller batch
2025-02-21 | redwood-raven-13b | q4_int8 | 1 | 128 | on | 26.7 | 110 | 250 | 0.005 | shorter seq + cache improved p95
2025-02-25 | redwood-owl-7b | q2_nf4 | 8 | 256 | on | 65.2 | 70 | 150 | 0.0017 | unstable memory on my node (OOMs once); watch mem use
2025-02-28 | redwood-owl-7b | q4_int8 | 4 | 512 | on | 22.5 | 140 | 420 | 0.0028 | doubling seq kills p95 despite cache; consider chunking prompts

Notes / interpretations:
- Prefix caching is the biggest single SLO win for p95 on our common prompt shapes (doc summaries). Keep it enabled for prod traffic when prefix reuse > 30%.
- Batching is great for tokens/s and cost, but watch tail latency; keep route-level policy that drops batch size for spikes above X concurrency.
- Quantization: q4_int8 is the best baseline for 7b on this hardware. q2_nf4 is tempting for cost but unstable on 1xA10 without more swap. Need to test on dedicated pool.

Micro action items (personal):
- [ ] Re-run q2_nf4 with 2x swap and memory cap to replicate OOMs (target 2025-03-05).
- [ ] Add a small script to capture per-request KV-hit rate (for prefix cache) — current numbers are eyeballed.
- [x] Try batch=4 first, fall back to batch=1 for p95 > 300ms (manual today, automate next week).
- [ ] Pin small test to Redwood console route config with a canary (ticket: JIRA-INF-219).

Open questions / hypotheses for next week:
- Does q4_int8 degrade delta-ROUGE on summarization tasks? Quick eval with 20 prompts to quantify.
- At what prefix reuse threshold does cache pay for itself on cost? Need to compute per-route ROI (tokens saved vs cache miss overhead).
- Can we safely enable q2_nf4 in Dedicated with autoscale? Maybe if burst capacity for OOMs exists.

Quick mini-calcs (notes):
- latency -> $/1k tokens rough: if tokens/s = T and p50 ~L ms, cost per 1k = base_gpu_hourly/ (T*3600/1000) — (I use experimental estimator below).
- Estimator used: hourly_est = $1.20 (dev box equiv); tokens_per_hour = tokens/s * 3600; cost_per_1k = hourly_est / (tokens_per_hour/1000). Numbers above rounded.

Logs / references:
- local run commands: ./run_infer --model redwood-owl-7b --quant q4_int8 --batch 4 --kv-cache on --seq 256
- quick slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CH12345/p1676200000000
- rough confluence note: CONF-serve/bench-notes-2025 (draft)

Random thoughts / heuristics (to save):
- If p95 < 200ms for batch 4 with cache on, call it "interactive-good".
- For routes with heavy doc prefix reuse (>50%), prefer larger batch + aggressive cache.
- If OOMs on q2_nf4, prefer q4_int8 + batch tuning; q2_nf4 only for dedicated multi-gpu pods.

End of sheet. Will keep appending runs and short notes; meant as quick single-file working log.
